content.html.title: Images and live content | PageCurl.Maui
content.html.summary: Images and live content Images Use PageTurnView when your application already supplies SKImage values. TurnView.FrontImage = currentPage; TurnView.UnderPageImage = nextPage; TurnView.PreviousPageImage = previousPage; TurnView.BacksideMode = PageBacksideMode.CustomContent; TurnView.BackImage = reverseSide; Keep assigned images alive. Before disposing or recycling an image set, cancel interaction and clear the image properties. The control never disposes your images. Use ContentScale="AspectFit" to preserve their proportions. If PreviousPageImage is absent, backward turns fall back to UnderPageImage. Supply both when the neighboring pages differ. Live MAUI views Set PageCurlView.FrontContent to a MAUI view. For a separate reverse side, set BackContent and choose BacksideMode="CustomContent". Mirrored and solid-color modes need no second view. After changing content in place, request a fresh capture: await Reader.RefreshSnapshotAsync(cancellationToken); The control retains the last successful image when capture fails. Handle SnapshotFailed to explain that state to the user. A completed refresh task is not proof of a new frame when the platform adapter reports failure through that event. Video A native video layer may not appear in a page snapshot. Keep a poster view beneath the player, or supply a poster as the curl content. The sample uses a bundled clip and still image; the library itself has no media-player dependency. Interaction settings LockedEdge or LockedAnchor chooses the stationary edge or pinned corner. PageChangeThreshold controls the travel required to commit on release. FlickEnabled allows a quick gesture to finish sooner. ReduceMotion completes releases and commands without settling animation. Use labeled navigation buttons as an alternative to gestures. Update the model from PageTurnCompleted for both paths. See the API reference for the properties exposed by each control.

contributing.html.title: Contributing and validation | PageCurl.Maui
contributing.html.summary: Contributing and validation Keep geometry and interaction in Core. Keep MAUI, Skia, dispatcher and device work in the adapter. Keep scene and media dependencies in the sample. Verify a change Read the repository requirements before changing behavior. Add a deterministic regression that fails before the fix, then run the relevant Core or neutral MAUI suite. Rendering and lifecycle changes also need native evidence. The Verify workflow runs deterministic tests, a fresh package consumer, validation-tool tests, native package checks and platform builds. The Documentation workflow builds this site, checks local links and retains the validated site artifact. Use the repository validation skills for explicit target commands. Record completed evidence under docs/validation/; do not infer a runtime pass from an unsigned build or a workflow definition. Build these docs From the repository root: bash tools/build-docs.sh The pinned local tool manifest selects DocFX. Output goes to .artifacts/site. Serve that directory to inspect the site before publishing. Run bash tools/publish-docs.sh to rebuild and publish it to the public PageCurl-docs repository. Its Pages workflow deploys those static files. The source repository uses a GitHub plan that cannot host Pages from a private repository; publication therefore uses your existing GitHub credentials. The site includes these curated guides and generated public API signatures. Historical logs, plans and device identifiers stay in the repository. Report an issue Include the package/commit version, target framework, OS and device model, reproduction steps, and the complete first build or runtime error. For visual issues, include a small sample and a screenshot of the active turn.

getting-started.html.title: Quick start | PageCurl.Maui
getting-started.html.summary: Quick start You need a .NET 10 MAUI application and the workload for your target platform. The repository pins the SDK and workload set in global.json. Reference the library The source repository currently requires access. Until a published package is verified, add a project reference to src/PageCurl.Maui/PageCurl.Maui.csproj from the cloned repository. You can also pack the projects into a local NuGet feed. The MAUI package depends on Core; your application does not need a separate Core reference. Register SkiaSharp Add the handler registration in MauiProgram.cs: using SkiaSharp.Views.Maui.Controls.Hosting; var builder = MauiApp.CreateBuilder(); builder.UseMauiApp<App>().UseSkiaSharp(); Display a live page Add the namespace and control to a XAML page: <ContentPage xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/dotnet/2021/maui" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2009/xaml" xmlns:curl="clr-namespace:PageCurl.Maui;assembly=PageCurl.Maui"> <curl:PageCurlView x:Name="Reader" PageAspectRatio="0.75"> <curl:PageCurlView.FrontContent> <Grid BackgroundColor="#FAF8F1" Padding="24"> <Label Text="First page" TextColor="#1C211F" /> </Grid> </curl:PageCurlView.FrontContent> </curl:PageCurlView> </ContentPage> The view stays interactive while flat. The control captures it after layout and uses that image during the turn. Give the control a nonzero layout size. Connect navigation Maintain the current index in your application. Change it only after a committed completion; cancelled turns leave it unchanged. using PageCurl.Core; Reader.PageTurnCompleted += (_, e) => { if (!e.Committed) return; pageIndex += e.Direction == PageTurnDirection.Forward ? 1 : -1; Reader.FrontContent = CreatePage(pageIndex); }; Use PageNavigationState to enforce first/last boundaries and connect labeled Previous/Next buttons through TryTurn. See the sample for complete wiring, including readiness and scene changes. Do not start another turn while required snapshots are unavailable. Read images and live content for backside and refresh behavior.

runtime.html.title: Runtime and lifecycle | PageCurl.Maui
runtime.html.summary: Runtime and lifecycle Use the UI thread Assign content and image properties, issue turn commands and refresh snapshots on the MAUI UI thread. Core geometry and interaction have no UI dependencies; the MAUI adapter and its dispatcher do. Own images deliberately PageTurnView borrows images. Your application must keep them alive until they are no longer assigned or used by an active turn. PageCurlView and PageSpreadView own their captured textures. They reject and dispose obsolete captures, retain a last-good frame on failure, and keep active turn textures stable until the turn ends. Handle cancellation and reuse Call CancelInteraction() when removing or recycling a view. It rolls back, stops settling and releases pointer ownership. Clear borrowed image references before disposing them. Handler teardown cancels active work and releases adapter-owned snapshots; a cancelled caller wait does not mean the underlying serialized capture has finished cleaning up. The controls reject delayed results from hidden, replaced or disconnected content. If you supply a custom snapshotter, honor cancellation, use the UI thread and transfer ownership of the returned image to the control. Commit once PageTurnCompleted reports direction and whether the turn committed. Advance the model only when Committed is true. Threshold-crossing events provide feedback; they do not change the current page. The sample routes gestures, buttons, reduced motion and haptics through this same completion path. Handle failed snapshots separately from successful navigation so the interface does not report a refresh that never happened.

spreads.html.title: Two-page spreads | PageCurl.Maui
spreads.html.summary: Two-page spreads PageSpreadView presents a left and right page. It captures the neighboring pages before enabling navigation. <curl:PageSpreadView x:Name="Book" PageAspectRatio="0.75" LeftContent="{Binding LeftPage}" RightContent="{Binding RightPage}" PreviousLeftContent="{Binding PreviousLeftPage}" PreviousRightContent="{Binding PreviousRightPage}" NextLeftContent="{Binding NextLeftPage}" NextRightContent="{Binding NextRightPage}" /> Sheet mapping Direction Turning front Revealed underneath Turning back Forward Right NextRight NextLeft Backward Left PreviousLeft PreviousRight The back is the adjacent page the sheet lands on. If you omit it, the control uses the selected mirrored or solid-color fallback. Commands and boundaries Use TryTurnForward() and TryTurnBackward(). Enable buttons from CanTurnForward and CanTurnBackward; these include snapshot readiness. Use PageSpreadNavigationState to decide whether a neighboring spread exists. Update the six content slots from a committed PageTurnCompleted event. Replacing content schedules capture of dirty slots. Call RefreshSnapshotAsync() for in-place edits. Explicit requests during a turn wait until it ends and preserve cancellation. See runtime rules for the UI-thread and lifecycle contract.
